page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register in the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall within the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with uncached large-block reads measuring 20.95 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression workloads, such as Passmark encryption and single-threaded gzip compression, also rank in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.sn1.large is its constrained memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 and its lower-tier processing speeds, which limit its utility for resource-intensive applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution times compared to shared-core instances, making it a stable option for low-demand, compute-bound tasks. Suitable workloads include lightweight web serving, basic background processing, small-scale Redis operations, and minor utility tasks that do not require high memory capacity or rapid disk I/O.
